chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated, saying: Al-Hakam ibn Maskin al-Thaqafi narrated to me from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, from Ja'id Hamdan, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, in the lowest coffin are six from the earlier [generations] and six from the later [generations]. As for the six from the earlier [generations]: the son of Adam who killed his brother, Pharaoh of the Pharaohs, the Samiri, the Dajjal whose book is [recorded] among the earlier [ones] but he emerges in the later [times], Haman and Qarun. And the six from the later [generations]: Na'thal, Mu'awiya, Amr ibn al-As, and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. The narrator forgot two [names].

key_terms.ابْنُ آدَمَ: The son of Adam (referring to Cain/Habyl)
key_terms.التَّابُوتِ الْأَسْفَلِ: The lowest coffin (a specific level or compartment in Hell)
key_terms.السَّامِرِيُّ: The Samiri (the idol-maker during Moses' time)
key_terms.الْآخِرِينَ: The later generations (people of more recent times)
key_terms.نَعْتَلُ: Na'thal (a title/name for Uthman ibn Affan)

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve people destined for the lowest level of Hell according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the concept of *al-Jahannamiyyun* (those destined for Hell), categorizing twelve key figures into two groups: the 'Six from the First' (ancient archetypes of tyranny and deviation) and the 'Six from the Later' (key political and religious opponents of the Ahl al-Bayt). This classification underscores the Shia scholarly view that the sins of Pharaoh and Cain are mirrored in the political and theological rivalries of the early Islamic period, particularly among those who opposed Imam Ali's authority. The omission of two names by the narrator highlights the oral transmission nuances in classical hadith literature, yet the core list remains central to understanding the hierarchy of sin in Shia eschatology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-60 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father (ra) narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil Khat’tab, on the authority of Al-Hikam ibn Meskin al-Saqafy, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Siabah, on the authority of Ja’eed Hamdan that the Commander of the Faithful (as) said,

“Indeed there shall be twelve people in the coffins at the lowermost levels of Hell. Six of them are from the people of the past, and the other six are from the latter times. The six from the people of the past are the son of Adam who killed his brother, the Pharaoh of pharaohs, Samiri, Dajjal, whose book is in the era of people of the past, but shall come back in the future, Haman and Qarun (Korah). The six from the people of the latter times are Na’thal (Uthman ibn Affan), Muawiyah, 'Amr ibn al-‘Aas, and Abu Musa al-Ash’ari.” The narrator forgot to mention the last two names.
